one_liner: mypyc: compiles type-annotated Python modules to CPython C extensions; about 1.5x geomean on unannotated code, 2.4-22x on tuned code.
what_it_does: mypyc ships with mypy (pip install 'mypy[mypyc]') and turns ordinary Python modules into C extension modules that still run on CPython and can import any library. You run `mypyc mod.py` or call mypycify([...]) in setup.py to build wheels; the same source still runs interpreted during development. It compiles a strict, gradually typed subset of Python: the code must type-check under mypy, and annotations are enforced at run time with TypeError.
how_it_is_fast: It compiles ahead of time to C through mypy's type information. Calls, names and attributes inside one compilation unit are bound early, with no namespace dict lookups. Classes become C extension 'native classes' with vtable method dispatch and slot-like attribute storage. Small ints, bools, floats and fixed-length tuples are unboxed, and many list, dict, str and int operations use type-specialised primitives. The optional librt package adds a growable typed array (librt.vecs.vec) and other primitives that only help compiled code. Generated C is built with -O3 by default (mypyc/build.py opt_level).
when_to_use: Pure-Python, CPU-bound application code that already has (or can be given) precise type annotations: object-heavy logic with method calls and attribute access, integer and float loops, list indexing

Whole-program compilation of a typed codebase shipped as wheels, the way mypy ships itself (the docs credit this for a 4x speedup), when you want a speedup without leaving CPython or its C-extension ecosystem
Replacing a hand-written C extension, or code you would otherwise move to Cython, with plain annotated Python that still runs interpreted for development
Short-lived CLI tools, where a JIT's warm-up would eat the gain; mypyc is AOT, so startup is not penalised
when_not_to_use: Unannotated code expecting a big win: in kostya/jit-benchmarks (mypyc 1.0.1, CPython 3.10.7) the gain was about 1.5x geomean over 10 programs (binarytrees 3.15x, brainfuck2 1.84x, mandelbrot 1.61x, but matmul 0.91x, pidigits and regexdna 1.00x), and knucleotide, revcomp and nbody produced no valid result (derived from page data)

Code dominated by exceptions, dataclass/attrs creation or hashing, or interpreted callers touching compiled objects: first-party microbenchmarks show catch_exceptions 0.48x, access_attr_from_interpreted 0.41x, dataclass_as_dict_key 0.74x, create_dataclass 0.90x

Code that relies on monkey patching or mocks of compiled functions, nested or conditional class/function definitions, arbitrary descriptors, __getattribute__/__delattr__/__index__ on native classes, generator expressions with lazy semantics, or `if __name__ == '__main__'`
Workflows that need pdb breakpoints, cProfile/trace hooks or inspect on hot code, since compiled functions trigger none of them
Deep recursion: compiled code does not check for stack overflow and can crash the process; the docs still call mypyc alpha software

integration.form: module (Python-to-C compiler; output is a C extension .so/.pyd per compilation unit)
integration.dependencies: mypy[mypyc] (setuptools) and a C compiler with CPython headers at build time (GCC/Clang on Linux, Xcode CLT on macOS, MSVC Build Tools on Windows); at run time mypy_extensions types are erased, and librt is needed only if the code imports librt
integration.min_toolchain: CPython 3.10+ (mypy 2.4.0 requires-python >=3.10); code must pass mypy type checking
integration.platforms: anywhere CPython builds C extensions: Linux x86-64/aarch64, macOS, Windows (mypy's own compiled wheels exist for these plus musllinux x86-64 and win_arm64); not PyPy
integration.thread_safety: Supports free-threaded CPython; since mypyc 2.3 most operations are memory-safe under races, but primitives may have different atomicity from CPython and librt vec is not race-safe
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — same CPython interpreter and libraries, but you must annotate code for a large win, rebuild per Python minor version (not abi3), and accept semantic differences (early binding, runtime type checks, unboxed ints lose bool identity)

gotchas: Harness flaw in the catalogued kostya/jit-benchmarks numbers: the nbody table lists 'Python3 MYPYC 0.0 s, 1 run, MaxMem -' as the fastest entry, above C and Cython. That is a failed run recorded as a time, not a result. knucleotide and revcomp also show '-' (no successful run). Only 10 of 13 programs have usable mypyc numbers.

Methodology note on the headline 22.36x richards, 10.42x hexiom and 7.86x deltablue: runbench.py times a different source for the compiled side. bm_*_mypyc.py (compiled_variant=True) swaps lists for librt vec[i64] and globals for Final instance attributes, while the interpreted baseline runs bm_*.py. Even the baselines carry mypyc-specific i64 annotations. These numbers show what tuned code reaches, not what an existing annotated program gets.

Calls between separately compiled units, or from interpreted code, fall back to the boxed Python calling convention and late binding, so compile hot paths as one unit. Caching bound methods in locals, a classic CPython trick, slows compiled code.

Open segfault reports in the mypyc tracker: #1186 (subclassing collections.defaultdict), #1198 (module-level __getattr__), #1209 (dataclass field annotation using a TYPE_CHECKING-only compiled class) and #1203 (native attribute access on free-threaded builds). `# type: ignore` in compiled code can produce bad code.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick mypyc when your code is already type-annotated and must stay standard Python on CPython. Cython reaches C speed more easily on numeric loops (it won most kostya programs on unannotated code) but needs cdef/cpdef or its own build model for top speed. Codon and Shed Skin are faster but compile a restricted Python to native binaries outside CPython, and PyPy is a separate runtime. Over Nuitka, mypyc gives larger gains on annotated object code (binarytrees 23.25 s vs 72.55 s in kostya).
verified_claims_summary: First-party tracking (mypyc-benchmarks runbench.py, interpreted vs compiled in separate subprocesses, slowest third of runs dropped) on CPython 3.13.1, Ubuntu 24.04.1 and an Intel Core i5-1145G7 (C compiler and flags not stated) reports 2.41x (nqueens) to 22.36x (richards, tuned vec variant) at mypy commit 1ca7337. The independent kostya/jit-benchmarks round (mypyc 1.0.1 against CPython 3.10.7 on a Ryzen 7 3800X in Docker, unannotated code) gives about 1.5x geomean with a 0.91x-3.15x range (derived from page data).
status_note: Very active (mypy 2.4.0 released 2026-10-01, commits daily) and MIT-licensed with PSF/BSD portions in lib-rt, but the docs still label mypyc alpha and recommend careful testing before production use.
